To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a hand exoskeleton with free-fingertips and free-palm design, and intrinsic adaptability, can be successfully controlled by means of EMG to provide bilateral robotic assistance in grasping tasks, and that this approach is promising for application in stroke hand rehabilitation.

the developed hand exoskeletal device is capable to assist in grasping tasks, and to provide robotic assistance to the impaired limb, based on real-time EMG estimation of the grasping forces exerted by the healthy limb.
a robotic hand exoskeleton, designed to be worn on the hand of a stroke patient for bilateral rehabilitation of grasp, was developed and successfully tested in healthy subjects and stroke patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an innovative hand exoskeleton that can be used in bilateral training for rehabilitation of hand grasping in stroke patients.
the design, development and evaluation of an EMG-driven robotic hand exoskeleton with free-palm and fingertip, for bilateral training of grasping in chronic stroke patients.
the development of an EMG-driven robotic exoskeleton for hand rehabilitation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed system has shown to be a promising tool for robotic-assisted bilateral rehabilitation of grasps, and it is a valid option for the development of a new generation of rehabilitation robots.
the developed hand exoskeletal device is a feasible solution to provide robotic assistance in grasping, and to support bilateral rehabilitation of the upper limb in stroke patients.

the developed system can be considered as a valid and reliable tool for bilateral rehabilitation of hand grasping in post stroke patients, and as a promising solution for clinical application in the near future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented EMG-controlled hand exoskeleton can be considered as a valid and promising tool for bilateral rehabilitation of grasp in stroke.

the developed hand exoskeletal device, driven by EMG, can be successfully applied to provide bilateral assistance in grasping tasks, and thus, can be used to perform robotic-assisted bilateral rehabilitation of grasps.

this study demonstrates that the robotic hand exoskeleton is able to provide effective robotic assistance for bilateral grasping rehabilitation, and that the proposed EMG control strategy allows to perform the assistance for a variety of grasping tasks with different grasping objects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EMG can be used for real-time control of a robotic device to assist in grasping of any graspable object, without the need of any sensor on the object or on the patient's hand.
a robotic exoskeleton for grasping can be designed to be adaptable to patient's hand, and can be driven by EMG, without the need of sensors for grasping force measurement.
EMG signals can be exploited to estimate grasping force, and to control a hand exoskeleton, for robotic bilateral rehabilitation of grasps.
